title: Introduce epochal sampling-lattice to collapse hotpath trace metadata
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: tracing instrumentation in high-QPS frontends is introducing measurable CPU and allocation pressure in the hotpath. Heavy metadata encoding and span object construction for every request causes ~22% tracer CPU at 10k QPS and ~480KB/sec allocation rate per instance in staging. We need a solution that keeps fidelity for debugging and tail analysis while drastically reducing allocation and CPU pressure on the hotpath.

Proposed solution: an "epochal sampling-lattice" that replaces expensive metadata construction with a tiny inline token (64-bit lattice hash + 8-bit hint) generated deterministically at ingress. The token is extremely cheap to compute (single FNV-like fold over a small set of hot fields) and stored in the request header. Heavy span metadata encoding, structured payload attachment, and enrichment steps are deferred and gated to off-hotpath workers only when the token indicates a candidate for capture (policy decided by adaptive controller).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Hotpath work: compute 8-byte lattice token using a deterministic fold of [route, auth_tenant_id, sampling-seed, early-error-bit]. No allocation, uses stack-local u64 ops. Attach as upstream header and as a lightweight SpanHint field.
- Defer heavy work: full JSON metadata, traces.wire encoding, stack traces, and large headers only processed when capture worker elevates token for storage.
- Adaptive decision: a sampling controller periodically estimates QPS and tail latency signals (p99/p999) and adjusts the lattice acceptance threshold per-tenant; low-noise tenants sampled less frequently. Controller outputs are small updates (epoch) pushed to proxies to change acceptance window — hence "epochal".
- Guarantees: best-effort correlation for tail-based analysis (we can reconstruct probable candidates by token) but will trade absolute completeness for much lower overhead.
- Failure modes: if controller puppet fails, default to conservative sampling (very low) to protect hotpath. We will ship a kill-switch and a canary gate.

Acceptance criteria / targets:
- Reduce tracer CPU usage on hotpath by >= 35% at 10k QPS in staging compared to baseline (tracer CPU 22% -> <= 14%).
- Reduce allocations attributable to tracer by >= 60% under same load.
- No regression in median request latency (p50 change <= 1ms). p99 tail change must be monitored; acceptable temporary <= +3ms with rollback plan.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged infra change: token generation only (no worker processing) — deploy to canary (5% traffic). Verify no latency regressions and token header present.
2) Enable controller in read-only mode to observe token distribution and candidate rates for 48h.
3) Deploy capture workers in staging with sampling threshold and run end-to-end capture pipeline to S3 and tracing backend. Validate end-to-end reconstruction.
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring checks gating progress (tracer CPU, allocations, p50/p99 latency, storage spend).

Instrumentation/metrics to add:
- tracer.hotpath.cpu_percent (per service)
- tracer.hotpath.alloc_bytes/sec (per service)
- lattice.token_rate (tokens/sec) and token_accept_rate (accepted tokens/sec)
- capture.worker.latency and worker.backlog
- sampling.controller.epoch_rate and per-tenant acceptance_threshold

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for token determinism across language SDKs (Go/Node/Python) and route permutations.
- Microbenchmarks for token compute vs baseline metadata encode.
- Load test in staging at 12k QPS with realistic mix; run allocation sampling and eBPF snapshots.
- Chaos test: controller unresponsive simulation to validate default conservative mode.

Security/Privacy considerations:
- Token is deterministic but not reversible to original payload (we will document hash scheme and rotate salt per-region). No PII included in folded fields.

Documentation and SDKs:
- Ship spec for lattice token encoding and SDK helpers (Go/Node/Python) under dev-resources/observability/lattice-spec.md. Provide integration snippet for proxy and ingress SDKs.
